quest.title: Into the Deepwater Murk
quest.description: The open day has finally arrived. This is undoubtedly a good chance to find some information. You and Paimon plan to act, and search for clues in the Fortress of Meropide...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... It's morning already... *yawn* Paimon still needs more sleep.

choices.text: Let's use some coupons to skip our shift this morning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait, look over there! Isn't that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's one of Lyney's cards!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see what's written on it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Maybe you haven't heard, but today is the monthly 'free day.' Everyone has the day off today, which makes it the perfect time to do some investigating."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "It's been a while since we last talked, have you been making any progress lately? Let's meet at our usual spot in the factory area before lunchtime. I have new information."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Today's our lucky day, we have the day off!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the sound of it, Lyney's been making progress with his investigation. Wonder what he's discovered...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, we still have some time before we meet up. Let's talk with the people here for a bit more before we go.

choices.text: It's been a while since we've contacted him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really are something, to be able to fall asleep like that and even sleep-talk the entire time... You scared Paimon half to death!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did I say anything I shouldn't have?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, but you kept mumbling things along the lines of "Paimon, don't take my Grilled Fish" and "Put down the Adeptus' Temptation now."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon talked with Sigewinne the entire time you were asleep. She seems like she's just a sincere nurse, and Paimon didn't notice anything unusual in the room... Are you sure we're not going off-track with the infirmary?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Are we really off-track, though? There are still a few weird things about the place.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That movable hatch on the ground, as well as the question Sigewinne asked Lourvine... And also, were they really talking about their meds before we walked in?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Oh, and was Lourvine and Jurieu's argument genuine, or were they just putting on a show?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, hear me out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you really are super thorough! All those tiny little suspicious things that Paimon didn't even pick up on... We've gotta give the info to Lyney!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Over the next few days, you and Paimon work at your stations as normal. During your shifts, however, you manage to find opportunities to write keywords relating to your suspicions on a piece of paper.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You manage to pass the slip to a busy Lynette as she happens to pass by. Her disguise is impeccable, and she does not even look at you or change her expression as she pockets the info.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: And finally, the promised ninth day arrives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, there are some people talking over there. Let's listen in on the conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Downcast Convict
dialogues.text: If you ask me, those pompous parasites on the surface act like they're all a bunch of aristocrats. Do any of them give half a hoot about a bunch of dogs like us?

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: Hey, speak for yourself, mate! I'm no dog!

dialogues.speaker: Downcast Convict
dialogues.text: Aww, you think you're special or something? If you're here, then you're just a convict like the rest of us! I've heard that even if you're released after serving your sentence, going back to life on the surface ain't any better. Once a criminal, always a criminal, we're marked for life.

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: Hmph, I don't buy that.

dialogues.speaker: Downcast Convict
dialogues.text: Hey, how cool would it be if the whole world was destroyed by a giant flood and everyone had to start over from nothing?

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: What kind of filthy bilgewater you spewing!? I have family up there! You best shut your sewer-hole with talk like that!

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: Listen, things ain't so great on the surface, but who says that you have to leave? I've heard that you can still stay here and work even after you've served your sentence. Not bad if you ask me!

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: Who wants to live in the ruddy overworld anyway!? Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Downcast Convict
dialogues.text: And what makes you think they'd want to hire someone like you? It's one of the great mysteries of the universe, how someone as useless as you is so confident...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, sounds like they're really unhappy about the overworld.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Paimon never heard anyone use the words "overworld" or "underworld" when we were living up there. Is it only something the inmates down here say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true.

choices.text: It's normal for convicts to be unhappy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a group of people over there, let's go listen in!
So I said, that's not a faucet... Hey, who're you two? Why'd you come over all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Sorry for eavesdropping, sounds like you were talking about something private.
What's the matter? Haha, they're just looking to join in on our fun, that's all.
Hey, don't pretend like it's okay for them to just interrupt us like that! Hmph... Fine, you're lucky we don't mind extroverts that much.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, you guys are really nice!
Haha, you hear that, Cuistot? We're nice!

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: Your expressions tell me you're looking to hear some juicy info, am I right? Hehe, but before that... It just so happens that I know you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Are we that famous?

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: You kidding? How often does anyone get a personal tour led by His Grace himself? Practically everyone was talking about it. Word has it that you also caused quite the kerfuffle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hehe... It was just a little mistake...
A little mistake, huh? I like the way you put it. You see, people with a good attitude can join our group anytime, unlike some of the others here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your group?

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: I'm Cuistot, and this is Laverune. People usually call us the "Bombshell Bros." But don't worry, we're not playing with bombs or anything, it's just that our information is always so explosive... and we blow minds on the regular.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... you two really like to gossip? You sure know how to embellish...

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: No, no! You don't get it. Knowing intelligence will make things better for you here. For example, knowing who's working with whom, who has the latest rumors, who's not getting along... Wouldn't you like to know all that?

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Ha, all this info is worth something, you know. You should prove you're worthy of it.

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: Don't mind him, Cuistot is always this way. Just play nice and say something to massage his ego.

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: (The welfare meals, talk about the welfare meals!)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We ate the most incredible welfare meal recently!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, right! That meal we had yesterday was super delicious. Paimon can still taste it whenever she closes her eyes!

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: ...Is that so? Heh. To tell you the truth, I've been helping out with making those welfare meals. I've been working as a kitchen assistant for about a month and a half now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So you're the one who made those delicious steaks... Amazing! You could be a professional chef!

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: You are correct. I am a true professional. In fact, I even went to culinary school. But enough about that.

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Since you like my cooking, I guess that means we share similar tastes. Listen carefully. This little bombshell will help you learn what's really going on here in the Fortress.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Huh? Did Laverune just wink at me? It seems he's saying... "Don't be upset, he's a good fellow.")

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Listen kids... The power structure within the Fortress is quite complicated. The overworlders couldn't care less about us down here, we're basically dogs to them.

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: You've already met the one person here you should never cross... The Duke, Wriothesley. He knows more than you think and if he doesn't care about something, then he often doesn't bother dealing with it.

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: Those who have the Duke's attention get all kinds of special perks, even better treatment in the infirmary!

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Ah, I know who you mean! It's that Jurieu character, right? I don't think there's anything useful about him at all. Why does he visit the infirmary practically every day? Is it normal for anyone to be going in and out of there so often? If you ask me, he's just faking it to get out of work.

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: But did you know that Jurieu was a talented researcher from the Fontaine Research Institute before he came here? There's no denying that...

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: I don't care if he was a researcher that could turn dirt into Mora, once you're in the Fortress of Meropide, you're just another inmate like everybody else.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ah, interesting. According to Cuistot, a person named Jurieu frequents the infirmary. I should take note of that.)

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Speaking of which, the last time I saw him he was passing by in the corridor with Lourvine. I also heard they started arguing in the library and got into a fight, right? Guess that's just how terrible of a guy he is...

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: You mean he hit a woman? Wow, I never imagined he was that bad...

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: But that Lourvine's also quite the odd one, you know. She's always gabbing away, got into a fight with a man, and she also got sent to the infirmary. Come to think of it, I always see her going to the sick bay every couple of days, too.

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: Wait a second, you don't think...

response.speaker: Cuistot
response.text: Do you think... Could it be that... They're secretly meeting there to go on dates? Huh, but it's really hard to imagine...

response.speaker: Laverune
response.text: After all, I do remember seeing Lourvine beat Jurieu to a pulp that one time and... We might be overthinking things.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So Jurieu had a confrontation with a girl named Lourvine, who also frequently visits the infirmary... I'll remember that, too.)

choices.text: Oh my archon I'd love to know, please tell me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, good to know. Do you have anything else to tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think. Sounds like you want to hear something a little more tantalizing.

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Oh, did you know that the Duke was also a convict in the Fortress of Meropide before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, are you serious!?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: That's right, the Duke was an inmate just like you and me. It seems he was exiled here for committing some crime. Who knows how he ended up rising up to become the warden though...

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: To go from an ordinary inmate to becoming the manager of the whole place... I'm not gonna lie, I kinda respect that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: By the way, do you happen to know anything about a "forbidden zone"?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: A "forbidden zone"? Hmm, sounds like something that someone just made up. I've never heard of that, where did you hear about it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's just a rumor we've been hearing, but no worries if you've never heard of it. Do you have anything else you can tell us?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Anything else? Hmm... Not that I can think of, but I'll be sure to tell you anything interesting I hear next time! You'll have to play a game of Genius Invokation with me first, though!

talks.objective: Go to the production zone to search for Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: That look in your eyes... You've found something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A little something, yeah.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, this is no time to be modest! Just tell him we've found a boatload of information!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oho, as expected of the legendary duo. You have my full and undivided attention.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You summarize your findings to Lyney...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: ...Huh, I'd have never guessed that myself. The rumors swirling about this place are unreliable after all, and Master Childe probably went missing because he found a way out...

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He is a Harbinger, after all... I suppose he's much more resourceful than I initially gave him credit for.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, this isn't enough for our final report to "Father." We need to find out Master Childe's exact whereabouts.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Father told me that even though Master Childe said that he was just coming to Fontaine for a vacation, he actually had some personal reasons. His agenda might be linked to his disappearance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The most important thing right now is to catch up to him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: His escape route is already flooded, so we'll have to task someone with professional diving skills to chase after him.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Well, when you put it that way, it's obvious that only Freminet would be up to the task.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bingo! Is he around?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: He's working today — coming here as a group would have attracted too much attention. I'll talk to him about it later.

choices.text: Please do. We're counting on you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It's the least I can do. We're all in this together, so it's only fair for us to fulfill our end of the bargain.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Honestly, I'm far more impressed by you guys managing to collect all this information right under Wriothesley's watchful eyes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, collecting information has always been our strong point!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: ...Now let me think. To find out more information, Freminet will have to re-trace Master Childe's original route...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: And if he's to do that, he'll have to set out on the next pipe-cleaning day at the earliest. That's six days from now... Hmm, and after that, he'll probably take another two or three days to return...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can even estimate how long it'll take for him to get back!?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We've been working together for a long time... We know each other's capabilities like the backs of our hands.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what say you to meeting here nine days from now? We'll be able to pick up Freminet while we're at it, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, and there's just one last thing we'd like your help with.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Though we can just sit back and wait for Freminet's report on Master Childe's whereabouts, we still need to make more progress on the investigation of the forbidden zone...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Freminet's no master of disguise, Lynette's still working on getting intel from the other areas, and I'll need to spend some time helping Freminet prepare for his diving mission. So... you are the only ones we can count on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you want us to do? Will it be hard?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, I won't call it "easy," per se, but I think you'll be able to pull it off.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Listen carefully. You'll need to find an excuse to get into the infirmary and investigate the room and environs.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You've mentioned several sketchy-looking people always meeting at the infirmary earlier, so it probably has something to do with the secret we're hoping to uncover. You've already met the head nurse, so she'll be less suspicious of you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Investigate the internal structure of the infirmary and any active dealings within, and pass those onto me alongside anything else you're able to discover.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But also, there's no need to take risks. Don't forget, safety always comes first!

choices.text: Sounds good. I'll give it my best shot.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: #Ah, my apologies, I just started rambling out of habit... It was almost as if I was talking to my younger {M#brother}{F#sister}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that's not a bad thing, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #But what if I'm the older {M#brother}{F#sister}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, then we'll head out as soon as we finish our prep!

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Let's go our separate ways for now, then. Don't forget, we meet here again in nine days. Stay safe.

choices.text: Did you only say that because I'm an amateur?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No, when it comes to intelligence gathering, I'd never consider you to be an amateur. Didn't you say it yourself? It's always been your strong suit.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I'll believe anything as long as it comes from you. So, please prove your prowess to me once again.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: No need to thank me! This was always a part of our mission, after all.

talks.objective: Enter the Infirmary to obtain intelligence

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Someone, please help! {M#He}{F#She}... {M#He}{F#She}'s sick!
Whoa, are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh my! What's wrong, little one? There's no need to panic — take a deep breath before you begin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} started complaining of a stomach ache, and then nausea, and then collapsed onto the ground... Paimon d—doesn't know what to do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Freezing limbs, twitching fingers, and pale complexion... Could it be poison...?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Let me take a look... Please lie down over here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oof... My stomach really hurts...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I'll get you to the bed safely. Here, hold onto my shoulder and walk slowly...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #*sniff*... You can do it, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Th—Thank you... I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Don't apologize! You're sick, after all. Now, please relax, I'm just going to do a preliminary check-up on you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sigewinne has taken out a few instruments and begun to do her check-up... I hope I'm not so healthy that she gets suspicious...)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, mmm. I see now.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #My check-up has confirmed that {F#she}{M#he}'s not in any mortal danger. That's our worst fear out of the way!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Ah, th—that's good, but...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'll continue my diagnosis of the patient now. Please relax and take a deep breath.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sigewinne's using her hands to palpate different areas on my abdomen... Seems like she's using elemental energy, too? Her expression's growing more and more relaxed...)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I don't sense serious damage to your organs, either. Does it hurt when I press here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I—It's not too bad.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: And here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Oof, that hurt a little...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Eh? But based on my initial check-up, there shouldn't be a problem here... How strange...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Oh no, was my acting a bit over the top?)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hmm... What about here? Does this hurt?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, not really, can barely feel it.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oh... Mmm, I understand. So that's what it is.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I think you just ate something that disagreed with you, that's all. Nothing too serious, outside of a pretty bad stomachache when it decides to act up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... So that's what it is... Thank goodness it's not anything more serious!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Mhm, and there've been other inmates complaining about the food recently. I'll inform our head chef Mr. Wolsey of this problem as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Congratulations, the health risk is incredibly low, so you should recover within a couple days. Why don't you take a rest here while I go get some medicine for you?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Miss Lourvine... I'll have to trouble you to help me look after this new patient while I'm gone.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Very well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, and she hopped away just like that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Phew, this infiltration mission is going much more smoothly than I imagined. Next... There are only two people left in the room.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sigewinne just called that woman "Lourvine," so she has to be one of those frequent visitors to the infirmary I've heard of before. Would that mean the man next to her is "Jurieu," then?)

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Hello... So how are you feeling now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still not great...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I can't keep staring at her, it'll draw unwanted attention... That guy also seems to have noticed, now he's looking in my direction, too.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{F#Her}{M#His} stomachache's really bad, {F#she}{M#he} was stumbling about the whole way here, so Paimon's really worried...

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: If Miss Sigewinne says it's not a serious problem, then there's no need to worry. She's the best medic we've got down here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it also looks like she's the only medic you've got down here...

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Ah, well... That's true.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "that's true"? That's really misrepresenting the situation. Of course I can't speak for the whole Fortress, but it's not like everyone imprisoned here is useless, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Though they may have committed crimes and gotten locked up here as a result, they still know a thing or two about medicine, and they help Miss Sigewinne take care of the sick and injured.

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Yeah yeah, you're right, but did you have to lecture me about it in front of another patient? Aren't you a patient too? Where did all your energy come from?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Uh... Ah, that's correct. Ahem... Sorry, I got a bit ahead of myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you two also sick?

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: We've been sick a while. I come back every once in a while for check-ups, and to pick up the medicines Miss Sigewinne prescribes for us, that's just the nature of chronic illnesses. As for her...

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Hah, you could say she fancies herself as Miss Sigewinne's capable helper because she learned a bit of medical knowledge ages ago.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Please watch your mouth, Mr. Jurieu. Don't forget that you are the primary reason I have frequent heart palpitations!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't start arguing now! Please, keep it civil at least...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (These two seem to have a pretty terrible relationship, and only ran into each other because they came here to pick up their meds at the same time.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...But outside of the two of them, there's nothing suspicious inside the room. All the files on the table appear to be patient records, and while there's a box... I can't check it out right now.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (There also aren't that many furnishings on the wall... Eh? Wait, there seems to be a movable hatch on the ground over there?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Hey, there's no need to fight! Everyone will be released someday, so there's no need to argue over silly things like this!

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: Hmph, release? It's way too early for us to even think about that! And who the heck knows if we'd even be able to continue our previous lives?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The presence of a movable hatch isn't strange by itself, but... perhaps it's my adventurer's intuition speaking, but isn't it a bit strange that there's a movable hatch here of all places?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is it... hiding something?)

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Please allow me to end this boring and useless conversation. Oh, and Mr. Jurieu, I don't want to see your face here again anytime soon!

dialogues.speaker: Jurieu
dialogues.text: And same to you, Miss Lourvine. Anyway, that was more than enough rest for me, so I'm going to get out of this excessively noisy place. See you later, everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He just slowly walked off like that...?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Hmph, that's just what he's like.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: I'm sorry you had to see all of that. I'm Lourvine, and that's... Well, his name is Jurieu, but I hope you'll never have cause to remember his name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really can't stand him, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: I mean, can you blame me? Who would like someone who's as arrogant and obsessed with weird research topics as he is? ...Ahem, but there's no need to keep dwelling on him.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: I—I'll accompany you two for a while... Miss Sigewinne should be back soon, and I'm sure you'll feel better as soon as you've had some of her medicine.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you for looking after me.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: No, no... It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm back~! Did you rest like you promised?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Thank you for getting our medicine, Miss Sigewinne.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Did you all cooperate with your bedrest? I trust that nobody got up to walk around? Good, here, this should be two days' worth of medicine for you. Take one pill now, and then continue your bedrest.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You take the stomachache pill that Sigewinne gave you.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Ahh, Miss Lourvine, I left in a bit of a hurry just now, do you still remember if we discussed the color of the pill that you should be taking today?

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: I remember. You said it should be yellow.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Did they talk about that before we walked in? Why don't I remember?)

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Yellow, huh... Hmm, I understand. These are yours — please make sure to go to bed early after taking them tonight. You'll benefit from a good night's sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Lourvine
dialogues.text: Alright, then I'll also be on my way now. I hope you feel better soon, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See ya!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: I'm going to fill out your medical record now. You're widely known as the Traveler, right? I just want to double check a few details, if that's alright with you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Those two made quite the commotion just now, so why don't we let {NICKNAME} rest? Paimon can answer the questions instead.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Mmm-hmm, so {F#her}{M#his} primary symptoms are abdominal pain, with secondary symptoms of nausea. Is there anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... That's it!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Alright then~!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything we should know, besides to take the meds?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #No, {F#her}{M#his} base constitution is quite good, so I'm sure {F#she}{M#he}'ll recover quite quickly after taking the medicine. Please make sure to stick to blander, less stimulating foods, and don't stay up too late at night.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Got it, Paimon will hold {NICKNAME} to that for sure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Sigewinne's still looking at me... I should just try to take a nap, like she said.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? You're going to take a nap already? ...Okay, then, you get some rest!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: (You move yourself to a regular patient's bed and relax completely. The weariness from work and intel-gathering that you've been holding back all this time overwhelm you at once.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: ...You can, however, still catch some hints of Paimon's conversation with Sigewinne.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Mhm, we've been to lots of places together! {F#She}{M#He} may look a bit under the weather now, but {F#she}{M#he}'s actually suuuuuper strong!

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: #Oh, so you're the best of companions. Don't worry, {F#she}{M#he} will recover soon.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: ...Companion. That word brings forth a wave of comfort. You let yourself relax and fall into a restful sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: ...Ah, you're awake.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How do you feel? You slept for a really long time, but we never left!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel a lot better. Thank you both.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Well, now you can go back without a worry in the world! Remember to take your meds regularly, and don't forget, bland foods!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mhm! Thank you, Miss Sigewinne!

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Hey, you over there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who, me?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Yeah, you! Say, do you like playing card games? You know, like Genius Invokation TCG!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You TCG players are like Mint in the wild. Literally sprouting up everywhere!

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Hey, c'mon now. What's wrong with finding fellow Invokation aficionados? Anyway, care to join me for a game?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No thanks, we're busy with other things at the moment.

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Oh, alright. No pressure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why would you be looking for people to play Genius Invokation in a place like this? Don't people usually come here to fight?

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Haha, whether you're throwing down cards or throwing punches, it's all a competition, isn't it? It's all the same in my eyes.

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: There are lots of card players here in the Fortress. When I saw you, I immediately thought: Hey, even outsiders from other nations play cards! So I came over to say hi.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Would you mind chatting with us for a moment?

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great, since you've been here longer than us, you need to flex your seniority a little bit, right? Maybe you could start by telling us newcomers some stories about this place.

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: I thought you would've already heard everything by now. Alright then, did you have anything specific in mind? Or do you want me to just pick a topic?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't you pick? We'll let you know if we've heard it already.

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Alright. Have you heard any strange rumors since you've arrived?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, we have.

response.speaker: Bavilliers
response.text: Then did you know that there are some people who're always gossiping over in the corner?

choices.text: Even people down here play that game?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You mean Cuistot and Laverune?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: Yes, so you've already met those two. Hahaha, they're quite a pair. They always keep an eye out for the latest happenings and gossip about everything. I've never seen anyone with more time on their hands...

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: I heard that they used to be a chef and a bartender before they were sent down here. You know how bartenders are... always chatting with customers. And chefs love to pass the time just hanging out when they're not cooking.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't know that.

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: There are two guys who are always skulking around in the corners of corridors gossiping. The bigger guy is Cuistot, and the skinny one is Laverune. People call them the "Bombshell Bros."

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: I never really found their gossip very "mind-blowing"... It's pretty much just the same stuff that I hear about when I'm at work every day.

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: If you're interested, you can go talk with them. They tend to talk a lot of nonsense, but they aren't exactly bad.

dialogues.speaker: Grumpy Convict
dialogues.text: Anyway, I've already decided to stay here.

dialogues.speaker: Downcast Convict
dialogues.text: *sigh* Wish I could say the same...

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: Is it really alright for us to talk about people behind their backs like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Laverune
dialogues.text: That's just how it goes, good gossip is still gossip.

dialogues.speaker: Cuistot
dialogues.text: Yeah, I guess you're right... But wait, we're not just gossiping, this is legit information we're discussing here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Bavilliers
dialogues.text: See ya later. Hey, let's play a game if you ever have time.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Seems like a lot of people have been coming down with an upset stomach lately... I'll need to address that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Today's the day! Let's go meet up with Lyney.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After doing some prep work with Paimon, you begin slowly approaching the infirmary under the guise of just meandering around aimlessly...
